name: Rick Nowels
notes: An LA writer-producer specialising in melancholy adult pop: 88–120 straight with the backbeat on 2&4 and ballads at 66–96, so the session runs 66–120. His most-used device is documented — "minor-verse-to-relative-major-chorus… i–VI–III–VII becoming I–V–vi–IV" — with "sustained pedal tones under changing chords", which is why both cycles are authored at equal weight and the harmonic rhythm sits on two bars. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick on 1 and the '&' of 3", "soft snare on the backbeat", and "16th filtered hats, tambourine from the chorus" — plus the mix instruction that governs the whole block: "**he leaves the drums quiet so the vocal sits forward**", which is the soft velocity tier and a −7 dB perc offset. The bass is "bass programming with a rounded sub on roots and long durations; a played bass enters for the chorus" — `mirror_kick` at 0.93. He plays guitar and keyboards on his own productions and writes fast in intimate settings, and his melodies are "conversational, narrow, and sit on chord tones, with a string arrangement supplying the counter-melody" — a narrow register at a high `chordToneBias` with the counter carrying the strings. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are every drum probability and `bpm.mode` 100. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“bass programming with a rounded sub on roots and long durations; a played bass enters for the chorus.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
